page: Microsoft Azure E2s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical execution core via hyperthreading, backed by 16.0 GB of system memory to maintain an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. Cache hierarchy configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes no local ephemeral storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and does not feature discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate balanced single-threaded processing alongside predictable constraints inherent to a single physical core. The single-core Geekbench score of 1629.0 and stress-ng score of 1889.98 sit within the median cloud distribution, supported by single-threaded gzip compression at 28.3 GB/sec. However, multi-core benchmarks such as multi-core stress-ng at 1931.64 and multi-core Geekbench at 1883.0 rank in the lower decile. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 14.0 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 13.26 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific tests reveal 2.01 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.5 GB/sec in static web throughput.

The E2s_v5 instance provides cost efficiency for deployments that necessitate a substantial memory footprint without consuming surplus CPU capacity. The primary tradeoff stems from its limited compute headroom and total absence of local NVMe storage, meaning compute-heavy operations and IOPS-intensive workloads will encounter architectural bottlenecks. The instance is structured for small relational databases, Redis or Memcached nodes, lightweight enterprise middleware, and staging environments managing memory-bound tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure E2s_v5 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core on an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor at 2.8 GHz. Configured with 16.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio alongside 48 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 support. The server contains no local storage, requiring network-attached disks, and lacks GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles indicate solid single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core reaching 1629.0 and gzip compression hitting 28.3 GB/sec, while multi-core metrics sit in the lower percentiles due to the dual-thread topology. Uncached memory throughput reaches 14.0 GB/sec read and 13.26 GB/sec write. This instance presents an efficient resource balance for small memory-intensive applications, low-volume database servers, in-memory caching tiers, and background processing workers that do not require high parallel compute density.
